paper.title: Allocating Human Oversight in AI-Enabled Analytics

settings.name_in_paper: Online human-validation allocation under PPI++ (adaptive Neyman allocation with unknown rectification difficulties)
unmapped: Each pull of unit q yields a paired observation (human label Y_q, LLM prediction Y_q^LLM); the objective is the terminal weighted variance sum_q w_q A_q / n_q of tuned PPI++ estimators, where A_q = Var(Y_q - lambda_q^* Y_q^LLM) is unknown
Per-unit sampling costs c_q and importance weights w_q are known to the learner; total cost budget B
Regret is the gap to the Neyman oracle allocation's terminal objective, not cumulative reward
Learner needs the ranges of Y and Y^LLM (R) and constants (V_min^LLM, M_Y, M_Y^LLM) to set the initialization K_0
Synthetic-data-rich regime: LLM-only pool size m_q -> infinity
settings.definition_quote: We model data collection as a sequential allocation process. At each step $t$, a policy selects a question $q_t\in\mathcal T$ based on past observations, collects one additional human response for that question (paying cost $c_{q_t}$), queries the LLM on the same covariates, and obtains one paired observation ... $\mathcal R(B):=\bE_{\pi}[\sum_{q=1}^Q w_q\frac{A_q}{n_{q,B}}]-\sum_{q=1}^Q w_q\frac{A_q}{n_q^*}$.

algorithms.name: UCB-Based Online Human-Validation Allocation with PPI++

symbols.T_max: floor(B / c_min), max number of labels
symbols.V_max: sum_q w_q A_q / K_init, worst-case terminal objective

conditions: Y_q and Y_q^LLM bounded almost surely (Assumption 1)
tuning: initialization K_init = ceil(K_0 ln(Q T_max/delta)) with K_0 depending on the assumption constants

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions~\ref{ass:boundedpp}--\ref{ass:nondeg_ppipp} hold. Run Algorithm~\ref{alg:ucb-time-indexed} with $K=\lceil K_0\ln(QT_{\max}/\delta)\rceil$ ... Then for all sufficiently large $B$, \mathcal{R}(B)\le O\left(\frac{\ln(QT_{\max}/\delta)}{B^2}\right)+\delta V_{\max}.

results.notes: Regret is terminal weighted-MSE gap to Neyman oracle allocation (quantity 'other'). Paper's Q (number of units) mapped to K; the paper's K (initialization) renamed K_init. The delta*V_max term is additive exact; O applies to first term. Constants depend on weights, costs, A_q.

conditions: Y_q and Y_q^LLM bounded almost surely (Assumption 1)
results.notes: Corollary part of the main theorem; Q, costs, weights and A_q treated as constants.
